extension_points.name: Obsidian community plugin API
extension_points.detail: <vault>/.obsidian/plugins/<id>/ (manifest.json + main.js); per vault. Plugins load only after the vault leaves restricted mode, a per-vault consent the app stores in its localStorage (enable-plugin-<appId>).
extension_points.source: known (checked against this app; not advertised by the bundle)

extension_points.name: Obsidian CSS snippets and themes
extension_points.source: known (checked against this app; not advertised by the bundle)

extension_points.name: Accessibility (AX) API
extension_points.detail: every app; needs the Accessibility permission, reads and drives the UI

caveats: Info.plist says version 1.8.4 but the state folder holds app-code archives (obsidian-1.13.7.asar); the running version may be the newest of those

routes.name: Obsidian CSS snippets and themes
routes.reason: the app reads it with no code of ours: <vault>/.obsidian/snippets/*.css, enabled in Settings > Appearance

routes.name: Obsidian community plugin API
routes.reason: the makers' extension point: can add UI and behaviour; <vault>/.obsidian/plugins/<id>/ (manifest.json + main.js); per vault. Plugins load only after the vault leaves restricted mode, a per-vault consent the app stores in its localStorage (enable-plugin-<appId>).

routes.name: URL schemes
routes.reason: deep links (obsidian://); trigger only. Caveat: `open` routes to an already-running instance, which may be the user's real profile

routes.name: Accessibility (AX) API
routes.reason: read and drive the UI; needs the Accessibility permission and acting through it is driving input, so ask first; the electron UI exposes a thin AX tree

routes.name: renderer script via DevTools Protocol
routes.reason: launch-time renderer script over the DevTools Protocol (--remote-debugging-port, lab profile, session only); app files untouched; check the app's terms first: a prohibition on client modification puts this out of scope; the Node inspect fuse is off (the main process is closed; the renderer port is a different door)

routes.name: network capture of the app's own traffic
routes.reason: your own account and data only; rarely needed for an app mod

routes.name: companion tool beside the app
routes.reason: rebuild the part you need next to the app, from its data files or API; most work, and the user sees it outside the app

routes.name: edit the app's files
routes.reason: editing a signed bundle breaks its seal: that defeats an integrity check; an updater would overwrite the edit anyway
